title: Tata Steel dips 7% as APL Apollo plunge on ₹28,000 cr deal; Hindalco under pressure - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Shares of Tata Steel fell sharply by 7.30 per cent to ₹165.00 on Monday, while APL Apollo plunged 17 per cent following the announcement that Tata Steel has approved the divestment of its tubes business and its entire equity stake in Tata Steel Colors, formerly Tata BlueScope Steel, to APL Apollo for an aggregate consideration of up to ₹280 billion.

Under the deal, the Tubes Business will be transferred for cash consideration of up to ₹117 billion, while the 100 per cent stake in Tata Steel Colors will be sold for ₹163 billion. Both transactions are inter-conditional and are expected to close simultaneously, subject to regulatory approvals, by March 31, 2028.

Tata Steel to acquire 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo for ₹15,510 crore

JM Financial has maintained a Buy rating on Tata Steel with a target price of ₹240, calling the transactions a significant value-unlocking exercise. The brokerage noted that the aggregate consideration represents approximately 31 per cent of Tata Steel’s September 2026 consolidated net debt of ₹914.23 billion, providing the company with meaningful financial flexibility and room to redeploy capital toward core steelmaking operations and balance-sheet strengthening.

Nifty hits 9-month high as IT, Auto lead gains; metal stocks drag

Meanwhile, Hindalco shares declined 1.79 per cent to ₹912.90, adding to broader pressure on the Nifty Metal index, which fell 2.96 per cent to 11,908.35, making it the worst-performing sectoral index in the session. The metal index has declined 9.62 per cent over the past three months and 10.30 per cent over six months. Among other decliners in the index, NMDC fell 2.45 per cent, SAIL dropped 2 per cent, and JSW Steel shed 1.81 per cent.

The broader market presented a mixed picture. While Nifty and Sensex gained over 2.6 per cent and 2,300 points respectively last week, Monday’s session opened positively before selling pressure pulled benchmark indices below their previous closing levels. IT stocks outperformed with gains over 1 per cent, while banking and metal stocks faced headwinds.
